adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:153 — Denials are cached for 30s with no invalidation on grant, so a newly granted user stays denied and the checked-first denial cache defeats the new "fall back to DB when the cache is outdated" path.

adjudication.rationale: In `Service.Check`, the new `permDenialCache` is checked first and causes an immediate deny (`if _, ok := s.permDenialCache.Get(...); ok { return Allowed:false }`). The denial entry is written whenever the DB-based check returns `!allowed` (`s.permDenialCache.Set(..., true)`). There is no invalidation/refresh path shown in this diff when permissions are later granted, so a previously denied (user,action,name,parent-folder) combination will continue to be denied until the cache entry expires. This also bypasses the new “fallback to DB when cache is outdated” logic because the denial cache short-circuits before any cached-perms/DB lookup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30 — Denial key joins name and parent with "_" even though UIDs may contain underscores, so (name "a_b", folder "c") and (name "a", folder "b_c") share one key and a denial of one wrongly denies the other.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:974 — "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" passes without the denial cache: the permCache entry is false (not a grant) and the empty fakeStore also denies, so the test cannot catch a broken denial path.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:137 — If cached permissions exist but deny, the code still increments the cache-miss metric, and on DB fallback it calls GetUserIdentifiers a second time, so the cache-usage metrics are misleading.

adjudication.rationale: In Service.Check, when cached permissions are found (err==nil) but `allowed` is false, the function falls through and unconditionally increments `s.metrics.permissionCacheUsage.WithLabelValues("false", ...)` (see the line after the `if err == nil { ... }` block). That makes the cache-usage metric count a cache hit (cached perms existed and were used to evaluate) as a "false"/miss unless it allowed. Also, for user/service-account identities, `getCachedIdentityPermissions` calls `s.GetUserIdentifiers(...)` to build the cache key; on fallback to `getIdentityPermissions` it will call `GetUserIdentifiers` again via `getUserPermissions`, causing duplicate identifier lookups on the deny/fallback path (even if `idCache` may make it cheap). This is metric/efficiency correctness rather than functional correctness.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:31 — Denial cache key joins name and parent with unescaped "_", so distinct (name, parent) pairs like ("a_b","c") and ("a","b_c") collide and one resource's cached denial wrongly denies another.
matched_golden_ids: The cache key construction in `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses simple string concatenation with underscores, which can lead to ambiguous keys and collision risks when any component contains underscores or is empty. This could result in incorrect denial cache hits, affecting user permissions.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag the same underlying problem: building the denial cache key by concatenating components with an unescaped underscore can create ambiguous keys and collisions (e.g., when components contain underscores), leading to incorrect cache hits and wrong permission denials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:153 — Negative results are cached per resource with no invalidation, so a denial keeps returning Allowed=false for up to shortCacheTTL after a grant or folder move, even when the permission cache is refreshed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `permDenialCache` and an early return in `Service.Check`: if `permDenialCache.Get(...permDenialKey...)` hits, it immediately returns `Allowed: false` without consulting `permCache` or the DB. The cache entry is set whenever a DB-backed check returns `!allowed` (`s.permDenialCache.Set(..., true)`). There is no code in the diff that clears/invalidate this per-resource denial key when permissions change or when an allow is later observed, so a previously cached denial can override newly granted access until `shortCacheTTL` expires (even if `permCache` is refreshed to include the grant).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:31 — The denial cache key leaves out the identity type, so different identity types with the same UID (e.g. anonymous/render with an empty or shared UID) share denial entries.

adjudication.rationale: The new denial cache key `userPermDenialCacheKey(namespace, userUID, action, name, parent)` (pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go) does not include `identityType`. In `Service.Check`, the denial cache is consulted *before* any identity-type-specific handling (`permDenialKey := userPermDenialCacheKey(... checkReq.UserUID ...)` and immediate deny on hit). Therefore, if two different identity types can produce the same `UserUID` string within a namespace (e.g., empty/shared UID), a denial cached for one identity type would incorrectly deny the other.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:342 — getCachedIdentityPermissions duplicates the identity-type switch and cache-key derivation (incl. a second GetUserIdentifiers call) from getIdentityPermissions/getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions, so cache lookup and cache population now live in separate functions that must be kept in sync by hand

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `getCachedIdentityPermissions` with its own `switch idType` and cache-key derivation (`anonymousPermCacheKey` / `userPermCacheKey`) and, for users/service accounts, it calls `s.GetUserIdentifiers` to compute the UID before looking up `permCache` (service.go: new function). On cache miss, `Check`/`List` then call `getIdentityPermissions`, which (as shown by existing functions) ultimately calls `getUserPermissions`/`getAnonymousPermissions` where cache lookup was removed and permission fetching/caching happens via singleflight/store. This splits the identity-type branching/key-derivation logic across multiple places and can lead to duplicated work (notably a second `GetUserIdentifiers` call on miss) and requires manual sync if keying/identity handling changes. This is a concrete maintainability/perf concern grounded in the diff, not an immediate correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:123 — Check duplicates the checkPermission error-handling/metrics block for the cached and uncached paths instead of resolving permissions once and running a single check

adjudication.rationale: In Service.Check, the diff adds an early cached-permissions path that calls s.checkPermission(...) and includes its own error logging and requestCount metrics increment/deny return (around the new block after getCachedIdentityPermissions). The uncached path later still calls s.checkPermission(...) with a similar error-handling/metrics pattern. This is real duplication introduced by the change; it’s a maintainability/refactoring concern rather than a verifiable functional defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30 — userPermDenialCacheKey reuses the ".perm_" prefix of userPermCacheKey with ambiguous "_" joins, so denial and permission keys share a namespace and can collide (e.g. action/name containing "_") in the shared cache

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go, userPermDenialCacheKey builds keys by concatenating fields with the same ".perm_" prefix as userPermCacheKey and using raw "_" separators: namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent. This makes the key mapping non-injective if any of action/name/parent can contain "_" (e.g., (action="a_b", name="c", parent="d") and (action="a", name="b_c", parent="d") produce the same string). Since these keys are used against a shared underlying cache (permCache/permDenialCache both wrap the same cache instance), such collisions can cause incorrect cache hits/overwrites and wrong allow/deny decisions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116 — Denial cache key is built from the raw checkReq.UserUID while permission keys use the resolved userIdentifiers.UID, an inconsistent keying scheme that makes invalidation reasoning harder

adjudication.rationale: In Service.Check, the denial cache key is built with checkReq.UserUID directly: `userPermDenialCacheKey(..., checkReq.UserUID, ...)`. However, permission cache lookups/building (e.g., `getCachedIdentityPermissions` and `getUserPermissions`) resolve `userIdentifiers` via `GetUserIdentifiers(...)` and then key permissions by `userIdentifiers.UID` (`userPermCacheKey(ns.Value, userIdentifiers.UID, action)`). The diff does show an inconsistent keying scheme between denial caching and permission caching, which can complicate cache invalidation/consistency if `checkReq.UserUID` is not always the canonical resolved UID. The diff alone doesn’t prove `checkReq.UserUID` can differ from `userIdentifiers.UID`, so this is a concrete design/edge-case concern rather than a verified functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:137 — permissionCacheUsage is reported "false" when cached permissions were found but did not allow, making the cache-hit metric misleading

adjudication.rationale: In Service.Check, after calling getCachedIdentityPermissions, if cachedPerms are found (err == nil) but checkPermission returns allowed == false, the code does not record a cache hit and falls through to `s.metrics.permissionCacheUsage.WithLabelValues("false", checkReq.Action).Inc()` before fetching from the DB. This reports a cache miss even though the cache was successfully read (it just didn’t contain an allowing scope), making the cache-usage metric misleading as described in the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:239 — NoopCache is exported (with unused receiver names "lc") though only used inside this file, widening the package API unnecessarily

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `type NoopCache struct{}` in `pkg/services/authz/rbac.go` with an exported name (capitalized). In this diff it is only instantiated within the same file (`authzlib.WithCacheClientOption(&NoopCache{})` in `ProvideAuthZClient`), so exporting it does unnecessarily expand the package’s public API surface. Also, the method receivers are named `lc` but never referenced inside `Get/Set/Delete`, which is a lint/style issue visible in the diff (though not a functional defect).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:367 — After removing the only cacheHit:true case, TestService_getUserPermissions keeps a cacheHit field and if-branches that are now dead code

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the only test case in `TestService_getUserPermissions` that explicitly sets `cacheHit: true` is removed. That makes it plausible that any `cacheHit`-driven branches in the test helper logic (and the `cacheHit` field on the `testCase` struct) are now unused/dead within this test, which is a maintainability issue rather than a product bug. However, the diff does not show the `testCase` struct or the conditional branches, so this cannot be fully confirmed from the provided hunk alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:139 — When cached permissions deny a Check, it falls through to getIdentityPermissions which no longer consults permCache, forcing a full DB permission reload for every newly-denied resource.

adjudication.rationale: In `Service.Check`, the new fast-path only returns early when cached permissions allow (`if allowed { ... return }`). If cached permissions evaluate to deny (`allowed == false`), it falls through to `getIdentityPermissions(...)`. The diff also removes the `permCache.Get(...)` checks from both `getUserPermissions` and `getAnonymousPermissions`, so `getIdentityPermissions` will hit the store even if `permCache` already contains the permission map. This is a concrete performance/caching-behavior change (though seemingly intentional to avoid stale-cache false negatives, mitigated later by `permDenialCache.Set(...)` after a DB-confirmed deny), not a correctness bug per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30 — Denial cache key includes resource name and parent folder, creating unbounded per-user-per-resource key cardinality in the shared cache.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `userPermDenialCacheKey(namespace, userUID, action, name, parent)` in `pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go` and uses it in `Service.Check` to cache denials (`permDenialCache.Set(...)`) and short-circuit future checks if the key exists. Because the key includes `name` and `parent` (resource-specific identifiers), it can create very high/unbounded key cardinality per user+action across many resources, which is a concrete cache scalability/eviction-pressure concern introduced by this change, not a direct correctness defect shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:103 — In-process authz client now uses NoopCache, removing the client-side 30s check cache so every access check goes through the full gRPC/service path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `ProvideAuthZClient` no longer calls `newRBACClient(channel, tracer)` and instead constructs `authzlib.NewClient(channel, authzlib.WithCacheClientOption(&NoopCache{}), ...)`. The added `NoopCache` implementation always returns `cache.ErrNotFound` on `Get`, effectively disabling the previous client-side local cache behavior for the in-process client. Remote clients still use a 30s `cache.NewLocalCache(...)` in `newRemoteRBACClient`. This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/architecture change (more calls traverse the gRPC/service stack) but not a verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:356 — On cache miss, GetUserIdentifiers is resolved twice per request (in getCachedIdentityPermissions and again in getUserPermissions).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `getCachedIdentityPermissions()`, which for `types.TypeUser`/`TypeServiceAccount` calls `s.GetUserIdentifiers(ctx, ns, userID)` to build `userPermCacheKey(...)`. On a permissions cache miss, `Check()` falls through to `getIdentityPermissions(...)`, which (via `getUserPermissions(...)`) calls `s.GetUserIdentifiers(ctx, ns, userID)` again. This is a redundant extra lookup per request path on cache miss (likely mitigated by `idCache`, but still unnecessary work), not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:153 — Denial cache entries are never invalidated, so a newly granted permission keeps being denied for up to shortCacheTTL (the stale deny short-circuits before any DB check).

adjudication.rationale: In `Service.Check`, the new `permDenialCache` is consulted first and hard-denies without any DB lookup: `if _, ok := s.permDenialCache.Get(...); ok { return Allowed:false }` (service.go ~113-121). Deny entries are added whenever the DB check returns not allowed: `if !allowed { s.permDenialCache.Set(..., true) }` (~150-153). There is no code in the diff that deletes/clears these deny entries on subsequent allows or permission changes, so once a deny is cached it will continue to short-circuit all checks for that (ns,user,action,name,parent) until the cache TTL expires, even if the permission is newly granted in the DB during that window.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:129 — An error from checkPermission on stale cached permissions becomes a hard failure instead of falling back to the fresh DB permissions path.

adjudication.rationale: In the new cached-permissions fast path in `Service.Check`, if `getCachedIdentityPermissions` hits and `s.checkPermission(ctx, cachedPerms, checkReq)` returns an error, the code logs and returns `deny, err` immediately (`return deny, err`) instead of falling back to `getIdentityPermissions` (DB) like it does when `allowed` is false. The diff does not show that “stale” cached permissions would actually cause `checkPermission` to error (staleness would more likely produce `allowed=false` and then it *does* fall back), but the finding is valid as an edge-case robustness concern: any cache-induced `checkPermission` error becomes a hard failure rather than trying the DB path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:137 — permissionCacheUsage records a "false" miss when cached perms exist but deny (or when the lookup errors), and records nothing for anonymous/render lookups, which skews the cache hit-rate metric.

adjudication.rationale: In `Service.Check`, the diff increments `permissionCacheUsage` as a miss (`"false"`) whenever cached permissions are present but `allowed` evaluates to false: after `getCachedIdentityPermissions` succeeds and `checkPermission` returns `allowed == false`, the code falls through to `s.metrics.permissionCacheUsage.WithLabelValues("false", checkReq.Action).Inc()` (new block around lines ~113–140). That skews the cache hit-rate metric because a cache hit that results in a deny is still a cache hit. However, the finding’s claim that it “records nothing for anonymous/render lookups” is not supported by the diff: `getCachedIdentityPermissions` returns `cache.ErrNotFound` for render-service and checks the anonymous key; `Check` then increments the miss metric in both cases, so it is recorded. This is an observability/metric-accounting issue rather than a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:356 — getCachedIdentityPermissions can hit the DB via GetUserIdentifiers and its error is dropped; the fallback then repeats the same failing DB lookup, doubling DB load while the DB is degraded.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, getCachedIdentityPermissions calls s.GetUserIdentifiers(...) for user/service-account identities and returns that error if it fails. However, Service.Check ignores any non-nil error from getCachedIdentityPermissions (it only uses the cached path when err == nil) and then unconditionally falls back to s.getIdentityPermissions(...), which (via getUserPermissions) will call GetUserIdentifiers again. This makes a DB failure in GetUserIdentifiers trigger two failing DB lookups per request, increasing load during degradation; the initial error is effectively dropped instead of being returned.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:103 — The in-process RBAC client now uses NoopCache and loses its 30s client-side cache, so every Check/List goes to the service and load increases.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `ProvideAuthZClient` (in-process client) changed from `newRBACClient(channel, tracer)` to `authzlib.NewClient(..., authzlib.WithCacheClientOption(&NoopCache{}), ...)` (rbac.go ~98-106). The removed `newRBACClient` previously configured a 30s `cache.NewLocalCache` client-side cache (the same code now lives only in `newRemoteRBACClient`). With `NoopCache`, the in-process client no longer caches authz responses, so repeated Check/List calls won’t be served from the client cache and will hit the in-process service handler each time. This is a performance/load concern, not a correctness defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30 — Denial cache key joins userUID/action/name/parent with unescaped "_" so distinct requests (e.g. name "a_b"+parent "c" vs name "a"+parent "b_c") collide, letting one cached denial wrongly deny a different resource

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `userPermDenialCacheKey(namespace, userUID, action, name, parent)` in `pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go`, which constructs a cache key by concatenating fields with unescaped underscores: `... + "_" + name + "_" + parent`. In `Service.Check` this key is used to short-circuit denies (`permDenialCache.Get` => immediately returns `Allowed: false`). Because neither `name` nor `parent` are escaped or length-delimited, different `(name,parent)` pairs containing underscores can produce the same key (e.g., `name="a_b", parent="c"` vs `name="a", parent="b_c"`), causing an incorrect cached denial to apply to a different resource.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30 — Denial keys share the "ns.perm_" prefix and underlying cache with userPermCacheKey entries, so crafted UID/action strings can alias across typed caches

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `userPermDenialCacheKey` using the same string prefix (`namespace + ".perm_"`) as `userPermCacheKey` (pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go), and `permDenialCache`/`permCache` are both `cacheWrap[...]` instances built on the same underlying `cache` (pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go, `NewService`/`setupService`). Because keys are constructed via raw concatenation with `_` separators and no escaping, different component tuples can produce identical final strings if any component can contain `_`, creating potential key collisions between the two caches (and even within `userPermCacheKey`). Whether UID/action/name/parent are actually craftable/underscore-containing isn’t verifiable from the diff, so impact/exploitability can’t be confirmed here, but the collision risk is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:117 — Denial cache is checked before any permission lookup and is never invalidated on grant/role/team changes, so newly granted access stays denied until TTL expiry

adjudication.rationale: In Service.Check, a permDenialCache entry is consulted first and immediately returns Allowed=false without checking permCache or the DB (new code around building permDenialKey and `if _, ok := s.permDenialCache.Get(...); ok { return Allowed:false }`). The denial cache is populated on any non-allowed result (`if !allowed { s.permDenialCache.Set(..., true) }`) and there is no invalidation mechanism in the diff besides TTL via `newCacheWrap[bool](..., shortCacheTTL)`. This introduces a new, verifiable behavior where a previously denied (and cached) decision will continue to deny even after permissions/roles/teams change until the TTL expires, because the DB is never consulted on a denial-cache hit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:154 — No test checks that a DB denial writes permDenialCache, or that a stale denial is cleared or bypassed once the user is granted access (a stale denial blocks for up to shortCacheTTL).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds negative-result caching in Service.Check: it consults permDenialCache first and returns Allowed=false immediately on a hit (service.go:113-121), and it writes to permDenialCache when the DB-backed check returns !allowed (service.go:150-153). The newly added tests cover (a) allow via cached permCache, (b) DB fallback on cache miss/outdated permCache, and (c) denying when an explicit permDenialCache entry exists, but they do not assert that a DB denial actually populates permDenialCache. Also, since permDenialCache is checked before any DB call, a stale denial entry will block access until TTL expiry, and there is no code path that clears/bypasses it on subsequent grants—this behavior is visible in the diff and is not tested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:1300 — TestService_CacheList only covers a cache hit; List's fallback to the DB on a cache miss and its error path when the cached lookup fails are not tested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:922 — The cache-miss and outdated-cache fallback tests assert only Allowed=true; they never check store calls or the cache usage metrics, so the cache path is not verified.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:239 — The new NoopCache and the in-process client wiring that turns off client-side caching have no tests.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `NoopCache` type in `pkg/services/authz/rbac.go` and changes `ProvideAuthZClient` to construct an in-process client with `authzlib.WithCacheClientOption(&NoopCache{})`, explicitly disabling client-side caching. The added tests in `service_test.go` cover server-side permission caching/denial caching (`permCache`, `permDenialCache`) but do not exercise `NoopCache` or the `ProvideAuthZClient` wiring that turns off client caching. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test concern for newly added behavior, not a directly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.
